newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firms seen buying rice, corn and wheat.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firms seen buying rice, corn and wheat.

text.p: Philippine grain importers are expected to be in the market for rice, corn and wheat this week if prices fall to lower levels, traders said on Monday.

"We expect the government to continue negotiations for rice importations ahead of the lean months of August to September this year and for more corn imports," said a senior trader in one of the country's largest food companies.
On Thursday, state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) signed a contract to buy 100,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China at $157 a tonne C&F, a senior Agriculture Department official said.
The deal was made through Top Glory Trading Co, representative of the National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corp of China, he said.
"Under the contract, the Philippine government was given an option to import an additional 10 percent of its actual order," said the official, who requested anonymity.
Of the total order, 60,000 tonnes corn will arrive between February 20 to March 20 and the balance between March 11 to 25 this year, the official added.
But traders said they expected livestock and poultry raisers to ask the NFA to import more corn to meet a projected supply shortfall of between 800,000 to one million tonnes this year.
"We are willing to pay a premium to be able to import corn (quickly) because of the lack of local supply," an official from the Philippine Association of Feed Millers Inc said.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said he expected Philippine corn imports to reach up to 500,000 tonnes this year.
The NFA said the average price of yellow corn his week increased to 10.60 pesos per kg from the previous 10.53 pesos while the price of white corn dropped to 11.06 pesos per kg from 11.11 pesos.
The average price of white corn at farm level increased to 6.70 pesos per kg from 6.63 pesos while yellow corn jumped to 6.78 pesos per kg from 6.58 pesos.
Traders and government officials also said the Philippines has started negotiations for the importation of rice from neighbouring countries.
In Bangkok, Thailand's Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn said on Thursday, after returning from a trip to Manila, that the Philippines is to buy 205,000 tonnes of 25 percent grade Thai rice.
Prachuab did not provide details on prices, but Thai sources said on Saturday the deal was done at $300 a tonne.

Grain traders from Vietnam also said they were expecting news to emerge soon of a possible deal between the Philippines and Vietnam, involving the purchase of as much as 200,000-300,000 tonnes of rice.
Minister Escudero said he expected the country to import between 300,000 and 500,000 tonnes of rice this year.

In the wheat market, traders said they expected Philippine flour mills to buy on price dips this week. "We may order for our March requirements if prices fall from current high levels in the United States," a trader in one of the country's largest flour mills said.
Philippine wheat buyers stayed out of the market last week due to high prices, traders said.
Conversion US$ =26.30
